ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, $AB$ is the diameter of circle $O$, $AC$ is a chord of circle $O$, $D$ is the midpoint of arc $BC$, and $DE$ is drawn perpendicular to $AC$ at point $E$, intersecting the extension of $AB$ at point $F$, and $DA$ is connected. If $AB=90\text{cm}$, what is the distance from the center $O$ to the "lever $EF$"?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $OD$,\\
since $D$ is the midpoint of the arc $BC$,\\
it follows that $\angle CAD=\angle BAD$,\\
since $OA=OD$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAD=\angle ADO$,\\
hence $\angle CAD=\angle ADO$,\\
since $DE\perp AC$,\\
it follows that $\angle E=90^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle CAD+\angle EDA=90^\circ$, which means $\angle ADO+\angle EDA=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $OD\perp EF$,\\
hence the length of $OD$ is the distance from the center $O$ to the "lever $EF$",\\
since $AB=90\text{cm}$,\\
it follows that $OD=OA=\boxed{45\text{cm}}$

图像描述：右侧几何图中有一个圆，圆心标为 O，水平直径 AB，其中 A 在圆的右端，B 在左端；C 位于右上方圆弧上，AC 是弦；D 位于上方偏左的圆弧上，并连接了 DA；过 D 的直线 EF 斜向右上，且在 E 处与 AC 垂直，向左延长后与 AB 的延长线交于 F。左侧是一个实物杠杆照片，主要用于说明“杠杆 EF”的背景，求解使用右侧几何图。

按解析坐标法推理：由 AB 是直径且 AB=90 cm，圆半径 R=45 cm。设圆心 O 为原点，A=(R,0)，B=(-R,0)。令 C=R(cos 2t, sin 2t)，对应右上方圆弧上一点。因为 D 是弧 BC 的中点，而 B 的圆心角为 pi，C 的圆心角为 2t，所以 D 的圆心角为 (pi+2t)/2=pi/2+t，因此 D=R(cos(pi/2+t), sin(pi/2+t))=R(-sin t, cos t)。

弦 AC 的斜率为 (R sin 2t-0)/(R cos 2t-R)=sin 2t/(cos 2t-1)=-cot t。由于 EF 垂直于 AC，所以 EF 的斜率为 tan t，可取方向向量为 (cos t, sin t)。而 OD 的方向向量为 R(-sin t, cos t)，与 EF 的方向向量点积为 R[(-sin t)(cos t)+(cos t)(sin t)]=0，所以 OD 垂直于 EF。又 EF 经过 D，因此从 O 到直线 EF 的垂线段就是 OD，其长度等于圆半径 R=45 cm。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the diagram, $AB$ is the diameter of circle $O$, $AC$ is a chord of circle $O$, $D$ is the midpoint of arc $BC$, and $DE$ is drawn perpendicular to $AC$ at point $E$, intersecting the extension of $AB$ at point $F$, and $DA$ is connected. If $AB=90\text{cm}$, what is the distance from the center $O$ to the "lever $EF$"?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect $OD$,\\
since $D$ is the midpoint of the arc $BC$,\\
it follows that $\angle CAD=\angle BAD$,\\
since $OA=OD$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAD=\angle ADO$,\\
hence $\angle CAD=\angle ADO$,\\
since $DE\perp AC$,\\
it follows that $\angle E=90^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle CAD+\angle EDA=90^\circ$, which means $\angle ADO+\angle EDA=90^\circ$,\\
it follows that $OD\perp EF$,\\
hence the length of $OD$ is the distance from the center $O$ to the "lever $EF$",\\
since $AB=90\text{cm}$,\\
it follows that $OD=OA=\boxed{45\text{cm}}$
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: On the left side of the figure is a photo of a physical lever/bracket, and on the right side is a geometric figure. In the figure on the right, the center of the circle is O, AB is the horizontal diameter passing through O, A is at the right end of the circle, and B is on the left side of the circle. Point C is at the upper right of the circle, and AC is a chord; point D is on the upper arc of the circle, and DA is connected. The straight line EF passes through D, is perpendicular to AC at point E, and after being extended leftward intersects the extension line of AB at F.

Reasoning: Connect OD according to the meaning of the problem. Because D is the midpoint of arc BC, arc BD = arc DC, so the inscribed angles subtending them are equal, namely ∠BAD = ∠CAD. Also because OA and OD are both radii of circle O, OA = OD, and triangle AOD is an isosceles triangle, therefore ∠OAD = ∠ADO. Since A, O, B are collinear, ∠BAD = ∠OAD, so ∠BAD = ∠ADO. Combining ∠BAD = ∠CAD, we can get ∠CAD = ∠ADO. Also because DE ⟂ AC, and E is on AC, in triangle ADE, ∠CAD and ∠EDA are complementary, namely ∠CAD + ∠EDA = 90°. Substituting ∠CAD = ∠ADO, we get ∠ADO + ∠EDA = 90°, therefore OD ⟂ DE. Since D, E, F are collinear, DE and EF are the same straight line, so OD ⟂ EF. Thus the distance from the center O of the circle to the “lever EF” is the length of the perpendicular segment OD. AB is the diameter and AB = 90 cm, so the radius OD = AB/2 = 45 cm.
